title: Embeddings: useful geometry, limited meaning
outcome: Interpret vector similarity without treating it as truth, identity, or permission.
cue: Near in a vector space is a clue, not a verdict.
version: Provider-neutral principles · Ruby 3.3 / Rails 7.2 lab · legacy Ruby 2.7 adaptation notes
useCase: Interpret vector similarity without treating it as truth, identity, or permission.
benefits: A clear decision and a way to check it.
drawbacks: Nearest is relative: every query has a nearest candidate even when none is relevant. Similarity values are not universal probabilities.

trace.title: Input and preprocessing
trace.detail:
## Understand

An embedding maps an input into a numeric representation. Training encourages some relationships to appear as useful geometry.

Similar wording or meaning may place vectors near each other, depending on the model and task.

A vector is not a compressed database row that can reliably be decoded back into every original detail.

Distance functions differ. Cosine distance compares direction; dot product and Euclidean distance have different behavior and normalization assumptions.

Use the distance recommended for the selected embedding model and evaluate retrieval on your data.

Keep embedding model/version, dimensions, preprocessing, and distance choice with the index. Vectors from unrelated embedding models generally cannot be mixed just because they have the same dimension.

A migration needs re-embedding or a deliberately validated compatibility strategy. Similarity does not establish factual support or authorization.

trace.title: Follow one input
trace.detail: Text → chosen embedding model → vector plus metadata → distance ranking → authorized relevant candidates. Evaluate whether the expected passage appears, not just whether the nearest score looks large.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Nearest is relative: every query has a nearest candidate even when none is relevant. Similarity values are not universal probabilities.
